subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
skillName: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
intro: This cluster test covers scale drawings (7.G.A.1), drawing geometric shapes with given conditions (7.G.A.2), and cross sections of three-dimensional figures (7.G.A.3). Choose the single best answer for each multiple-choice item.

items.prompt:
A map uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 6\text{ km}$. Two towns are $8\text{ cm}$ apart on the map. What is the actual distance between the towns?
A) $48\text{ km}$
B) $14\text{ km}$
C) $\frac{4}{3}\text{ km}$
D) $2\text{ km}$

steps: Each $1\text{ cm}$ on the map stands for $6\text{ km}$, so multiply the map distance by $6$.
$8 \times 6 = 48$, so the actual distance is $48\text{ km}$.
B) $14\text{ km}$ adds $8 + 6$ instead of multiplying.
C) $\frac{4}{3}\text{ km}$ divides $8 \div 6$, inverting the scale direction.
D) $2\text{ km}$ subtracts $8 - 6$ instead of using the scale.

items.prompt:
A blueprint uses the scale $1\text{ in} : 4\text{ ft}$. A wall is $20\text{ ft}$ long. How long is the wall on the blueprint?
A) $5\text{ in}$
B) $80\text{ in}$
C) $24\text{ in}$
D) $16\text{ in}$

steps: To go from actual length to drawing length, divide by the scale factor: $20 \div 4$.
$20 \div 4 = 5$, so the wall is $5\text{ in}$ on the blueprint.
B) $80\text{ in}$ multiplies $20 \times 4$, the wrong direction.
C) $24\text{ in}$ adds $20 + 4$.
D) $16\text{ in}$ subtracts $20 - 4$.

items.prompt:
On a scale drawing, a segment $3\text{ cm}$ long represents an actual length of $15\text{ m}$. What is the scale of the drawing?
A) $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ m}$
B) $1\text{ cm} : 45\text{ m}$
C) $1\text{ cm} : 12\text{ m}$
D) $3\text{ cm} : 5\text{ m}$

steps: Find how many meters one centimeter represents by dividing: $15 \div 3 = 5$.
So $1\text{ cm}$ represents $5\text{ m}$, giving the scale $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ m}$.
B) $1\text{ cm} : 45\text{ m}$ multiplies $15 \times 3$ instead of dividing.
C) $1\text{ cm} : 12\text{ m}$ subtracts $15 - 3$.
D) $3\text{ cm} : 5\text{ m}$ does not reduce the ratio to a unit scale of $1\text{ cm}$.

items.prompt:
A rectangular garden is drawn $5\text{ cm}$ by $8\text{ cm}$ using the scale $1\text{ cm} : 3\text{ m}$. What is the actual area of the garden?
A) $360\text{ m}^2$
B) $120\text{ m}^2$
C) $40\text{ m}^2$
D) $39\text{ m}^2$

steps: Convert each side to actual length: $5 \times 3 = 15\text{ m}$ and $8 \times 3 = 24\text{ m}$.
Find the actual area: $15 \times 24 = 360$, so the area is $360\text{ m}^2$.
B) $120\text{ m}^2$ scales the drawing area $40\text{ cm}^2$ by $3$ instead of by $3^2 = 9$.
C) $40\text{ m}^2$ uses the drawing area $5 \times 8$ without applying any scale.
D) $39\text{ m}^2$ scales only one dimension, using $15 \times 24$ but reading the wrong product.

items.prompt:
Can a triangle be drawn with side lengths $4\text{ cm}$, $5\text{ cm}$, and $11\text{ cm}$?
A) No, because $4 + 5 < 11$
B) Yes, because all three lengths are positive
C) Yes, because $5 + 11 > 4$
D) No, because the sides are not all equal

steps: For a triangle, the sum of the two shorter sides must exceed the longest side.
The two shorter sides are $4$ and $5$: $4 + 5 = 9$, which is less than $11$, so no triangle is possible.
B) is wrong because positive lengths alone do not guarantee a triangle.
C) tests the wrong pair; you must compare the two shortest sides against the longest.
D) is wrong because triangles do not need equal sides.

items.prompt:
Can a triangle have interior angles measuring $40^\circ$, $60^\circ$, and $90^\circ$?
A) No, because the angles sum to $190^\circ$
B) Yes, because each angle is less than $180^\circ$
C) Yes, because it has a right angle
D) No, because the angles must sum to $360^\circ$
items.answer: A) No, because the angles sum to $190^\circ$

steps: The interior angles of a triangle must sum to exactly $180^\circ$.
$40 + 60 + 90 = 190^\circ$, which is not $180^\circ$, so no such triangle exists.
B) is wrong because each angle being under $180^\circ$ is not enough; the total must be $180^\circ$.
C) is wrong because having a right angle does not fix the total.
D) uses $360^\circ$, which is the angle sum of a quadrilateral, not a triangle.
solution.answer: A) No, because the angles sum to $190^\circ$

items.prompt:
A triangle is described by two sides of $6\text{ cm}$ and $8\text{ cm}$ with an included angle of $40^\circ$ between them. How many triangles meet these conditions, and which criterion applies?
A) Exactly one triangle, by SAS
B) More than one triangle, by AAA
C) Exactly one triangle, by ASA
D) No triangle, because the angle is too small
items.answer: A) Exactly one triangle, by SAS

steps: Two sides with the angle between them is the side-angle-side (SAS) condition.
SAS fixes the triangle completely, so exactly one triangle (up to congruence) results.
B) AAA applies only when three angles and no side are given.
C) ASA requires two angles and the included side, not two sides and an angle.
D) is wrong because a $40^\circ$ included angle produces a valid triangle.
solution.answer: A) Exactly one triangle, by SAS

items.prompt:
A set of conditions gives the three interior angles $50^\circ$, $60^\circ$, and $70^\circ$ with no side length specified. How many triangles satisfy these conditions?
A) More than one, because the angles fix the shape but not the size
B) Exactly one, because the angles sum to $180^\circ$
C) None, because three angles cannot define a triangle
D) Exactly two, because of the ambiguous case
items.answer: A) More than one, because the angles fix the shape but not the size

steps: Check the angle sum: $50 + 60 + 70 = 180^\circ$, so a triangle is possible.
With no side length given, this is the AAA condition, which fixes the shape but allows any size.
Infinitely many similar triangles satisfy these angles, so more than one triangle results.
B) is wrong because a valid angle sum alone does not pin down the size.
C) is wrong because the angles do define a family of similar triangles.
D) confuses this with the ambiguous SSA case, which requires two sides and a non-included angle.
solution.answer: A) More than one, because the angles fix the shape but not the size

items.prompt:
A right rectangular prism is $6\text{ cm}$ long, $4\text{ cm}$ wide, and $3\text{ cm}$ tall. A plane slices it parallel to its top and bottom faces. What is the cross section?
A) A $6\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ rectangle
B) A $6\text{ cm}$ by $3\text{ cm}$ rectangle
C) A square
D) A triangle
items.answer: A) A $6\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ rectangle

steps: A slice parallel to the top and bottom faces matches those faces exactly.
The top and bottom faces measure $6\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$, so the cross section is a $6\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ rectangle.
B) uses the height $3\text{ cm}$, which is not exposed by a horizontal slice.
C) is wrong because the two dimensions $6$ and $4$ are unequal, so it is not a square.
D) is wrong because slicing a prism parallel to a face gives a rectangle, not a triangle.
solution.answer: A) A $6\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ rectangle

items.prompt:
A right rectangular pyramid is sliced by a vertical plane that passes through the apex and is parallel to a pair of base edges. What two-dimensional figure results?
A) A triangle
B) A rectangle
C) A trapezoid
D) A smaller similar rectangle

steps: A plane through the apex meets the base along a line segment and rises to the single apex point.
The cross section therefore has the base segment plus the apex, forming a triangle.
B) and D) describe slices parallel to the base, not through the apex.
C) a trapezoid comes from an oblique slice that misses the apex and crosses all four lateral faces.

items.prompt:
A right rectangular prism is $7\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$. A plane slices it parallel to the $7\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ face. What is the area of the cross section?
A) $28\text{ cm}^2$
B) $16\text{ cm}^2$
C) $112\text{ cm}^3$
D) $15\text{ cm}^2$

steps: A slice parallel to the $7\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ face is congruent to that face.
Its area is $7 \times 4 = 28$, so the cross section is $28\text{ cm}^2$.
B) $16\text{ cm}^2$ multiplies the wrong pair $4 \times 4$.
C) $112\text{ cm}^3$ computes the volume $7 \times 4 \times 4$ in cubic units, not a 2D area.
D) $15\text{ cm}^2$ adds dimensions instead of multiplying.

items.prompt:
A right rectangular pyramid has a base $10\text{ ft}$ by $6\text{ ft}$. A plane slices it parallel to the base exactly halfway up the height. What are the dimensions of the cross section?
A) A $5\text{ ft}$ by $3\text{ ft}$ rectangle
B) A $10\text{ ft}$ by $6\text{ ft}$ rectangle
C) A $5\text{ ft}$ by $3\text{ ft}$ triangle
D) A $20\text{ ft}$ by $12\text{ ft}$ rectangle
items.answer: A) A $5\text{ ft}$ by $3\text{ ft}$ rectangle

steps: A base-parallel slice of a pyramid is a smaller rectangle similar to the base.
At half the height, every linear dimension is scaled by $\frac{1}{2}$: $10 \times \frac{1}{2} = 5$ and $6 \times \frac{1}{2} = 3$.
So the cross section is a $5\text{ ft}$ by $3\text{ ft}$ rectangle.
B) keeps the full base size, ignoring that the cross section shrinks with height.
C) names a triangle, but a base-parallel slice gives a rectangle, not a triangle.
D) doubles the dimensions instead of halving them.
solution.answer: A) A $5\text{ ft}$ by $3\text{ ft}$ rectangle
